# C5 — Static-stability model

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | **SUPPORTED WITHIN STATED LIMITS** — Evidence supports the statement as worded, at its evidence class only. |
| Strongest accepted evidence | MODEL ONLY |
| Evidence classes cited | SPECIFICATION, IMPLEMENTATION, TEST PROCEDURE, ANALYTICAL |
| Gate reached | SOFTWARE REPRODUCTION (next: SYNTHETIC TEST) |
| Last review | CURRENT — human recorded 2026-11-14 by chief weapons engineer |

**Question.** Does the modeled rocket keep a static margin of 1.5-2.0 calibers through the motor burn?

**Current statement.** Revision 3 of the model corrects the reference formulation: the fin CP sweep term now uses the tip leading-edge sweep and the normal-force term the mid-chord line (the revision-2 script used the root chord and sweep length there, inflating the margin to a false 1.55-1.57 cal); the ellipsoid nose CP is derived (L/3) instead of assuming the ogive 0.466L; canards are modeled; the motor is the certified G64W; dry mass comes from an explicit component model. At the pre-resize geometry the true margin was about 0.7 cal (under-stable). Main fins were resized to 160 x 220 mm rectangles at 440 mm, and the nose carries a 250 g warhead simulator: the margin is 1.69 cal at ignition rising to 1.78 cal at burnout, inside 1.5-2.0. An independent strip-integration cross-check agrees with the closed form within 0.001 mm. All MODELED; no physical CG or mass has been measured.

## Assumptions

- The design-point component masses describe the intended rocket.
- A Barrowman static margin is the quantity the 1.5-2.0 cal target refers to.
- Subsonic flight only (max about Mach 0.2); no compressibility correction applied.

## Limitations

- A static margin does not establish dynamic stability or flight readiness.
- Component masses are authored estimates with stated sources; none has been weighed.
- The strip-integration cross-check validates the algebra, not the physics.

## Measurement needed to close the next gate

- An inert balance-point measurement of the assembled airframe's dry CG (compare to PRED-C5-DRY-CG).
- As-built fin and mass measurement once hardware exists.

## Pre-registered experiments

- None.

## What this claim does not establish

- Any inert physical measurement: none has been accepted for this claim.
- Physical performance of any hardware.
- Flight readiness or safety for live propulsion.
